summary.short: Would require deployers and developers of automated decision tools, AI used for consequential decisions such as employment, housing, health care, financial services and criminal justice, to document impact assessments by 1 January 2025, give affected persons notice, and not use tools that result in algorithmic discrimination.
summary.long: The bill would add Chapter 25 to the Business and Professions Code on automated decision tools: AI systems developed or marketed to be a controlling factor in consequential decisions such as employment, housing, health care, financial services and criminal justice. Deployers must perform, and developers must document, impact assessments by 1 January 2025 and annually, and assessments go to the Civil Rights Department within 60 days. Deployers must notify affected persons and, where a decision rests solely on the tool, accommodate requests not to be subject to it if technically feasible. Developers must give deployers documentation on known limitations and training data. Both must maintain governance programs and publish policy summaries. Deployers may not use tools that result in algorithmic discrimination; from 1 January 2026 a person may sue a deployer for compensatory damages, declaratory relief and fees, and public attorneys may seek injunctive relief after 45 days' written notice, which may be cured. The Civil Rights Department may impose administrative fines of up to $10,000 per violation. Deployers with fewer than 25 employees are excluded from assessment and governance duties unless the tool impacted more than 999 people per year.

notes: The document is the bill text only: it has no bill number, version label or legislative history, so the failed/dead stage comes from registry metadata, not the text. Section numbers are run together in the source, and numbering is taken from the text as presented. Inconsistency to note: Sec. 22756.1(d) exempts deployers with fewer than 25 employees, but 22756.1(b) imposes the developer assessment duty with no size exemption. Sec. 22756.4(c) also exempts small deployers, but the exemption is conditional on the deployed-tool threshold of more than 999 people per year. The private right of action in 22756.6(b) starts 1 January 2026, while the civil penalty in 22756.7 runs from the Civil Rights Department, and the text gives no standalone effective date for the act.
